A title proper is normally the basis of the value of a has authorized access point of manifestation element. Stipulations​ Use the element super-type to record a less specific relationship. Apply the stipulations for the element super-type unless indicated otherwise. Examples Property Value has title proper "90 vjet Bibliotekë Kombëtare" [Full example: 90 vjet Bibliotekë Kombëtare ​(2011; Biblioteka Kombëtare e Shqipërisë; object).] Property Value has title proper "The biographical dictionary of Scottish women" [Full example: Biographical dictionary of Scottish women ​(2007; Edinburgh University Press; volume; perfect binding).] Record a value that is selected from one or more values of the element super-type. Use the following order of preference: The title that is made most prominent by typography in the manifestation. The title that is the fullest. The title that is in the same language or script as the spoken word, tactile text, or text content that is embodied in the manifestation. The title that is given in the language or script of choice of the cataloguing agency. The title that appears first in a prominent manifestation statement when there is no collective title. The title that appears in the manifestation that embodies the expression of the earlist issue or iteration of a diachronic work that is known to the cataloguing agency. Examples Property Value has title proper "Was mir behagt, ist nur die muntre Jagd" [Full example: Was mir behagt, ist nur die muntre Jagd ​(2021; Carus; volume; full score). There is no collective title; the value is the first prominent title.] Property Value has title proper "The Paris apartment" [Full example: Paris apartment ​(2022; HarperCollinsPublishers; volume; case binding). The value is the only title that appears in manifestation statements.] Property Value has title proper "Voyage extraordinaire au coeur de l’atome + Voyage extraordinaire aux limites de l’univers" has title proper "Voyage extraordinaire aux limites de l’univers + Voyage extraordinaire au coeur de l’atome" [Full example: Voyage extraordinaire au coeur de l’atome + Voyage extraordinaire aux limites de l’univers ​(1996; Editions Casterman; volume). The manifestation has a tête-bêche layout that embodies two expressions with distinct titles that have equal prominence in statements of title and responsibility.] Property Value has title proper "Journal of construction automation and robotics" [Full example: Journal of construction automation and robotics ​(2022-; Korean Society of Automation and Robotics in Construction; online resource). The value is in the language of the cataloguing agency.] Record a value that includes a name of an agent or a title of edition that is integrated linguistically with a title that appears in a statement of title and responsibility. Examples Property Value has title proper "Report of the Expert Group on Special Care for Babies" Property Value has title proper "The post-humous works of Robert Hooke" Property Value has title proper "Charles Aznavour présente ses plus grands succès" Property Value has title proper "The compact edition of the Oxford English dictionary" Property Value has title proper "鲁迅全集" For a manifestation that embodies cartographic moving image, moving image, performed movement, or three-dimensional moving image content, record a value that omits a name that is integrated linguistically with a title that appears in a statement of title and responsibility and that is the name of an agent who is associated with the creation of the content. Examples Property Value has title proper "Star wars" Property Value has title proper "Thief" For a manifestation that embodies notated music, performed music, or tactile notated music content, and if there is no distinctive title in the statement, record a value that includes a type of composition and the key, numbering, date of composition, or medium of performance that appear in a statement of title and responsibility. Examples Property Value has title proper "String quintet no. 1, A major, op. 18" Property Value has title proper "Sinfonia 1 (1970)" Property Value has title proper "降B大调第一弦乐五重奏, 作品第K174号" For a manifestation that has a media type of "computer", and if no title appears in the manifestation or external sources of information, record the filename. Examples Property Value has title proper "notes23.txt" For a manifestation that has a super-unit, and if no specific title of the unit appears in any statement of title and responsibility or external source of information, or if the specific title is dependent on a common title of the super-unit, record a value that is a compound title. Examples Property Value has title proper "Dick’s picks, volume one, Tampa Florida 12/19/73" [A title of the sub-unit is the place and date of a recorded music performance.] For a manifestation that is an aggregate, record a value that is a collective title that appears in a statement of title and responsibility. Examples Property Value has title proper "The Black Lizard big book of locked-room mysteries" [Full example: Black Lizard big book of locked-room mysteries ​(2014; Vintage Books; volume; perfect binding).] Property Value has title proper "كليلة ودمنة" [Full example: كليلة ودمنة ​(1973؛ الشركة الوطنية للنشر والتوزيع؛ مجلد؛ غلاف مقوى).] Property Value has title proper "Wind, pinball" [Full example: Wind, pinball ​(2015; Harvill Secker; volume). The collective title proper appears on the spine of a volume that embodies two novels in a tête-bêche layout.] Property Value has title proper "Synthesis lectures on data, semantics, and knowledge" [Full example: Synthesis lectures on data, semantics, and knowledge ​(2021-; Morgan & Claypool Publishers; volume).] For a manifestation that is an aggregate, and if no collective title appears in any statement of title and responsibility or external source of information, record a distinct value of the title that appears first in a statement of title and responsibility. For a manifestation that embodies the expression of a diachronic work, record a value that omits designations of issue or iteration from a common title that appears in statements of title and responsibility in manifestations that embody issues or iterations of the work. Examples Property Value has title proper "Report on the … Conference on Development Objectives and Strategy" Property Value has title proper "La sidérurgie française en …" Property Value has title proper "IFLA series on bibliographic control" [[Full example: IFLA series on bibliographic control ​(2004-2012; De Gruyter Saur; volume).] For a manifestation that embodies the expression of a diachronic work, do not record a value that is an insignificant change from an earlier common title. An insignificant change includes: a difference in the representation of a character, word, ideograph, or punctuation mark, including abbreviation or expansion, spelling, and grammar a difference in the presence or absence of a character, word, or ideograph that expresses grammatical relationship, including articles, prepositions, and conjunctions a difference in the presence, absence, or order of characters, words, ideographs, or punctuation that are associated with the name of a collective agent or a kind of diachronic work a difference in the presence, absence, or order of characters, words, ideographs, or punctuation that indicates the same subject coverage of the diachronic work that is embodied by the manifestation If there is a significant change from an earlier common title, consider the manifestation to embody the expression of a new diachronic work and to be distinct from the earlier manifestation. See also: Manifestation boundaries For a manifestation that embodies an expression of an issue or iteration of a diachronic work, record a value that includes designations of issue or iteration in a common title that appears in a statement of title and responsibility. Examples Property Value has title proper "Mojo 357" [Full example: Mojo 357 ​(2023; H Bauer Publishing Ltd; volume).] Property Value has title proper "Report on the 2nd Conference on Development Objectives and Strategy" Property Value has title proper "Orkney archaeology review 2021"

The identifier is a catalogue number of the manifestation.] Apply the stipulations for the element super-type unless indicated otherwise. Веренадського; том). The value is a normalized ISBN that appears in a statement of identifier and terms of availability in the manifestation.] Record a value that appears in an authority file. Record a single occurrence of the element that is selected from one or more values that are associated with the manifestation. Use any order of preference. Record additional occurrences of the element, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Examples Property Value has identifier of manifestation "9788789035912" has identifier of manifestation "078903591X" [Full example: Knitting the Semantic Web ​(2007; Howarth Information Press; volume). The values are normalized 13 and 10 digit ISBNs that appear in a statement of identifier and terms of availability in the manifestation.]

rdfs:domain isbdm:Manifestation ; rdfs:subPropertyOf <http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbdm/elements/P1111> ; rdfs:isDefinedBy <https://www.iflastandards.info/ISBDM/elements/> ; dcterms:status "Published" . <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <rdf:RDF xmlns:rdf="http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#" xmlns:rdfs="http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#" xmlns:owl="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#" xmlns:dcterms="http://purl.org/dc/terms/" xmlns:isbdm="http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbdm/elements/" xmlns:ifla="http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbd/terms/"> <rdf:Property rdf:about="https://www.iflastandards.info/ISBDM/elements/P1117"> <rdf:type rdf:resource="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#DatatypeProperty"/> <rdfs:label xml:lang="en">has numeric designation</rdfs:label> <rdfs:comment xml:lang="en">Relates a manifestation to a nomen that is an identifier that includes numbers or alphabetic characters to indicate a position in a sequence of units of a multiple unit manifestation or of iterations of a diachronic work.</rdfs:comment> <rdfs:domain rdf:resource="http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbdm/elements/Manifestation"/> <rdfs:subPropertyOf rdf:resource="http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbdm/elements/P1111"/> <rdfs:isDefinedBy rdf:resource="https://www.iflastandards.info/ISBDM/elements/"/> <dcterms:status>Published</dcterms:status> </rdf:Property> </rdf:RDF> Additional information​ A manifestation may be associated with more than one numeric designation in different languages, scripts, or sequences. See also: has chronological designation String encoding schemes​ For a manifestation that embodies the expression of a diachronic work, a string encoding scheme should combine values for manifestations that embody expressions of issues or iterations of the diachronic work. Numeric designation SES is a string encoding scheme suggested by ISBD for Manifestation for a value of this element. Stipulations​ Use an element super-type to record a less specific relationship. Apply the stipulations for the element super-type unless indicated otherwise. Record a value that is based on a designation in a statement of issue or iteration that appears in the manifestation or an external source of information. For manifestation that embodies an expression of an issue or iteration of a diachronic work, record a value that is a numeric designation of only the issue or iteration. Examples Property Value has numeric designation "Issue 357" [Full example: Mojo 357 ​(2023; H Bauer Publishing Ltd.; volume + audio disc).] Property Value has numeric designation "Volume 3, issue 3" [Full example: Quantum world ​(2016; Reed Business Information Ltd; volume).] For a manifestation that embodies the expression of a diachronic work, record a value for the manifestation that embodies an expression of the first issue or iteration of the work in a numeric sequence, followed by punctuation to indicate an open sequence. Examples Property Value has numeric designation "Issue 1-" [Full example: Mojo ​(1993-; H Bauer Publishing Ltd.; volume + audio disc).] Property Value has numeric designation "Heft 1-" [Full example: Journal für Facility Management ​(2009-; Technische Universität Wien‏; online resource).] For a manifestation that embodies the expression of a diachronic work, and if there is a change in the sequence of numeric designations of issues or iterations, record a value that uses a string encoding scheme to combine: a value for the manifestation that embodies an expression of the first issue or iteration of the work in the old numeric sequence a value for the manifestation that embodies an expression of the last issue or iteration of the work in the old numeric sequence a value for the manifestation that embodies an expression of the first issue or iteration of the work in the new numeric sequence Record a has note on nomen associated with manifestation element that gives information about the change, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. For a manifestation that embodies the expression of a diachronic work that is known or assumed to have terminated, record a value that uses a string encoding scheme to combine: a value for the manifestation that embodies an expression of the first issue or iteration of the work in the numeric sequence a value for the manifestation that embodies an expression of the last issue or iteration of the work in the numeric sequence

rdfs:domain isbdm:Manifestation ; rdfs:subPropertyOf <http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbdm/elements/P1274> ; rdfs:isDefinedBy <https://www.iflastandards.info/ISBDM/elements/> ; dcterms:status "Published" . <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <rdf:RDF xmlns:rdf="http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#" xmlns:rdfs="http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#" xmlns:owl="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#" xmlns:dcterms="http://purl.org/dc/terms/" xmlns:isbdm="http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbdm/elements/" xmlns:ifla="http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbd/terms/"> <rdf:Property rdf:about="https://www.iflastandards.info/ISBDM/elements/P1234"> <rdf:type rdf:resource="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#DatatypeProperty"/> <rdfs:label xml:lang="en">has access point of manifestation</rdfs:label> <rdfs:comment xml:lang="en">Relates a manifestation to a nomen of the manifestation that is constructed using a string encoding scheme in an authority file.</rdfs:comment> <rdfs:domain rdf:resource="http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbdm/elements/Manifestation"/> <rdfs:subPropertyOf rdf:resource="http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbdm/elements/P1274"/> <rdfs:isDefinedBy rdf:resource="https://www.iflastandards.info/ISBDM/elements/"/> <dcterms:status>Published</dcterms:status> </rdf:Property> </rdf:RDF> Additional information​ An access point of a manifestation is assigned by a cataloguing agency and constructed by applying a string encoding scheme to the values of attributes and relationships of the manifestation. Element values​ The value of an access point is a literal string (a nomen string). Record a value that is: a string that is an access point that appears in an authority file a string that is constructed with a string encoding scheme an IRI for the access point that appears in an authority file String encoding schemes​ A string encoding scheme should construct the base access point from a value of a has title of manifestation element or element sub-type. The scheme should omit leading articles and punctuation so that the base appears in a browse index in order of the first significant word. If no value of a has title of manifestation element is available, a string encoding scheme should construct the base access point from a title that is assigned by a cataloguing agency. A string encoding scheme should use values of the following elements as qualifiers of a base access point: has category of carrier element has publisher agent element or element sub-type has date of publication element A string encoding scheme should use values of any elements as qualifiers, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Stipulations​ Use the element super-type to record a less specific relationship. Examples Property Value has appellation of manifestation "Catalogue of shipwrecked books (2018; William Collins; volume; case binding)" [Full example: Catalogue of shipwrecked books ​(2018; William Collins; volume; case binding). The value is an access point of the manifestation.] Use an appropriate element sub-type to record a more specific relationship. Apply the stipulations for the element super-type unless indicated otherwise. Record a single occurrence of the element that is selected from one or more values that are associated with the manifestation. Use the following order of preference: Nomen that is an authorized access point of the manifestation Nomen that is a variant access point of the manifestation Record additional occurrences of the element, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. If the access point does not appear in an authority file, record a value that is constructed with a string encoding scheme. For an access point that is based on a title of the manifestation, and if no title appears in any statement of title and responsibility in the manifestation or in external sources of information, record a value that is based on a title that is assigned by a cataloguing agency. An assigned title should be concise and reflect the distinctive characteristics of the manifestation or its embodied content. An assigned title should be consistent with a language and script of the embodied text or a language and script that is preferred by the cataloguing agency. Record a has note on nomen associated with manifestation element that indicates that the title is assigned.

Element values​ Record a value that is: a string that is an authorized access point that appears in an authority file a string that is constructed with a string encoding scheme an IRI for the authorized access point that appears in an authority file Record a value that is selected from one or more values of the element super-type. Use the following order of preference: The access point that is unique to the manifestation. An access point that is qualified with the most information that is available. String encoding schemes​ A string encoding scheme should construct the base access point from a value of has title proper element. The scheme should omit leading articles and punctuation so that the base appears in a browse index in order of the first significant word. If no value of a has title proper element is available, a string encoding scheme should construct the base access point from a title that is assigned by a cataloguing agency. If no value of a has title proper element is available, and if there is only one item that exemplifies the manifestation, a string encoding scheme should construct the base access point from a title that is assigned to the item by an owner. Examples Property Value has authorized access point of manifestation manifestation "Pogled na Akademijin vrt (195-; Mujadžić, Omer, 1903-1991; sheet)" [Full example: Pogled na Akademijin vrt ​(195-; Mujadžić, Omer, 1903-1991; sheet). The manifestation embodies a painting that does not include a signature, title, caption, or other text.] A string encoding scheme should use values of the following elements as qualifiers of a base access point: has binding element has category of carrier element has date of creation of manifestation element or element sub-type or has date of copyright of manifestation element has publisher agent element or element sub-type A string encoding scheme should use values of any elements as qualifiers, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. For a manifestation that embodies an expression of an issue or iteration of a diachronic work, a string encoding scheme should construct the base access point from a compound title that consists of a common title and a designation and title of the sub-unit or iteration, and use a value of a has category of carrier element as a qualifier. Stipulations​ ✽ If one or more authorized access points are assigned to the manifestation, record at least one occurrence of the element. Use the element super-type to record a less specific relationship. Apply the stipulations for the element super-type unless indicated otherwise. For a manifestation that embodies an expression of an issue or iteration of a diachronic work, record a value that includes a common title, a designation and title of the sub-unit or iteration, and a category of carrier. Examples Property Value has authorized access point of manifestation "New scientist. The collection. Volume 3, issue 3 [volume]"

Agent is an entity that is defined in the IFLA Library Reference Model as "An entity capable of deliberate actions, of being granted rights, and of being held accountable for its actions". Collective Agent is an entity that is defined in the IFLA Library Reference Model as "A gathering or organisation of persons bearing a particular name and capable of acting as a unit". Person is an entity that is defined in the IFLA Library Reference Model as "An individual human being". Collective Agent and Person are entity sub-types of Agent. A person is an agent; a collective agent is an agent. A collective agent comprises more than one person.

Use a relationship element to record an access point, identifier, or IRI value of a related entity that is supplied by a cataloguing agency. The value supports the general principles of "accuracy", "sufficiency and necessity", "significance", "economy", "consistency and standardization", "integration", and "interoperability" of Statement of international cataloguing principles ​(ICP).

Record a relationship element if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata, unless indicated otherwise. Record a value for an entity that is named or otherwise identified in a statement that appears in the manifestation. Record a value for an entity that is associated with the manifestation in external sources of information. Record an entity that is probably associated with the manifestation. Record a has note on entity associated with manifestation element that indicates the uncertainty. Record an entity that is associated with the manifestation. Do not record an entity that is known to be falsely associated with the manifestation. Record an entity that is real and is known to exist or have existed. Do not record an entity that is known to be fictitious. Record a has note on entity associated with manifestation element that gives information that is not recorded in a relationship element, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. If more than one entity is associated with the same relationship of the manifestation, record a separate occurrence of the element for each distinct value that is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Use the following order of preference: The prominence of names or titles of entities that appear in statements in the manifestation. The order of names or titles of entities that appear in a statement in the manifestation. The predominance of entities that are given in external sources of information. For a manifestation that embodies the expression of a diachronic work, and if there is a change in the information that is given in statements that describe the manifestation and appear in manifestations that embody expressions of issues or iterations of the work, record an additional occurrence of the element for the entity that has changed, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. For a manifestation that embodies the expression of a diachronic work, record a has note on entity associated with manifestation element that gives information about a change of entity that is related to the manifestations that embody expressions of issues or iterations of the work, including identification of the issue or iteration in which the change first appears, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. For a manifestation that embodies the expression of a diachronic work, record a has note on entity associated with manifestation element that gives general information about multiple changes over time of entities that are related to the manifestations that embody expressions of issues or iterations of the work,including identification of the issues or iterations in which the changes occur, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. See also: has note on entity associated with manifestation

Nomen is an entity that is defined in the IFLA Library Reference Model as "An association between an entity and a designation that refers to it". The designation is an appellation of an instance of the entity: a string that is used to reference the instance in a specific scheme or context. The string is labelled as a "nomen string" to distinguish it from other strings. An appellation or nomen string includes a name, title, access point, or identifier of an entity. The same nomen string may be associated with different instances of different entities; an instance of an entity may be associated with different nomen strings. Each unique combination of instance and nomen string is a distinct nomen.

Place is an entity that is defined in the IFLA Library Reference Model as "A given extent of space". Time-span is an entity that is defined in the IFLA Library Reference Model as "A temporal extent having a beginning, an end and a duration".

Expression is an entity that is defined in the IFLA Library Reference Model as "A distinct combination of signs conveying intellectual or artistic content". Item is an entity that is defined in the IFLA Library Reference Model as "An object or objects carrying signs intended to convey intellectual or artistic content". Work is an entity that is defined in the IFLA Library Reference Model as "The intellectual or artistic content of a distinct creation". A related manifestation is a manifestation that is distinct from the manifestation.

Use a manifestation statement element to record a string value that is transcribed from the manifestation. The value supports the general principle of "representation" of Statement of international cataloguing principles ​(ICP).

[Full example: RDA toolkit ​(2020-; RDA Copyright Holders; online resource). The values appear on the home page and About page respectively. The home page statement is the most prominent; the About page statement is considered to have utility for users of the metadata.] Property Value has manifestation statement of title and responsibility "Einstein on the beach, an opera in four acts by Philip Glass / Robert Wilson" has manifestation statement of title and responsibility "Set and light design, Robert Wilson; music - lyrics, Philip Glass [Full example: Einstein on the beach ​(2016; Opus Arte; videodisc; DVD). The values appear on successive screens of credits. The first two credits are considered to be the most prominent statement, and the remaining credits are considered to have utility for users of the metadata. The values concatenate the successive credits. Whitespace between credits is replaced by a vertical bar "|" and whitespace within credits is replaced by a comma-space.] If a statement of title and responsibility that appears in the manifestation is lengthy, record a value that includes the first five or six words or ideographs and that omits part of the statement from the middle or end, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Examples Property Value has manifestation statement of title and responsibility "Evangelistarium Marci Maruli Spalatensis …, opus uere euangelicum cultissimoque adornatum sermo, sub Fidei, Spei et Charitatis titulis, in septem partitu libros" For a manifestation that embodies cartographic image, cartographic tactile image, cartographic tactile three-dimensional form, cartographic three-dimensional form, still image, tactile image, tactile three-dimensional form, or three-dimensional form content, and if no distinct statement of title and responsibility appears in the manifestation, record a value that is a transcription of text that is embedded in the image or form. Examples Property Value has manifestation statement of title and responsibility "I am a jolly huntsman, My voice is shrill and clear" [Transcription of the first two lines of a poem.]

Scope note Domain Manifestation Range Literal Element sub-type has manifestation statement of editionhas manifestation statement of extenthas manifestation statement of identifier and terms of availabilityhas manifestation statement of issue or iterationhas manifestation statement of publication, production, manufacture, or distributionhas manifestation statement of categoryhas manifestation statement of title and responsibility URI https://www.iflastandards.info/ISBDM/elements/P1025 Type DatatypeProperty Status Published { "@context": { "rdf": "http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#", "rdfs": "http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#", "owl": "http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#", "skos": "http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#", "dcterms": "http://purl.org/dc/terms/", "ifla": "http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbd/terms/", "isbdm": "http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbdm/elements/" }, "@graph": [ { "@id": "https://www.iflastandards.info/ISBDM/elements/P1025", "@type": [ "rdf:Property", "owl:DatatypeProperty" ], "label": { "en": "has manifestation statement" }, "description": { "en": "Relates a manifestation to a statement that appears in a manifestation to represent aspects of itself." }, "domain": { "@id": "http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbdm/elements/Manifestation" }, "isDefinedBy": { "@id": "https://www.iflastandards.info/ISBDM/elements/", "label": "ISBD Manifestation elements" }, "status": { "label": "Published" } } ] } @prefix rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> . @prefix rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> . @prefix owl: <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#> . @prefix dcterms: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/> . @prefix skos: <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#> . @prefix isbdm: <http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbdm/elements/> . @prefix ifla: <http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbd/terms/> . <https://www.iflastandards.info/ISBDM/elements/P1025> a rdf:Property, owl:DatatypeProperty ; rdfs:isDefinedBy <https://www.iflastandards.info/ISBDM/elements/> ; dcterms:status "Published" . <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <rdf:RDF xmlns:rdf="http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#" xmlns:rdfs="http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#" xmlns:owl="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#" xmlns:dcterms="http://purl.org/dc/terms/" xmlns:isbdm="http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbdm/elements/" xmlns:ifla="http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbd/terms/"> <rdf:Property rdf:about="https://www.iflastandards.info/ISBDM/elements/P1025"> <rdf:type rdf:resource="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#DatatypeProperty"/> <rdfs:label xml:lang="en">has manifestation statement</rdfs:label> <rdfs:comment xml:lang="en">Relates a manifestation to a statement that appears in a manifestation to represent aspects of itself.</rdfs:comment> <rdfs:domain rdf:resource="http://iflastandards.info/ns/isbdm/elements/Manifestation"/> <rdfs:isDefinedBy rdf:resource="https://www.iflastandards.info/ISBDM/elements/"/> <dcterms:status>Published</dcterms:status> </rdf:Property> </rdf:RDF> Additional information​ This element supports the user task to identify the manifestation. The same statement may be repeated in different languages or scripts in the manifestation. Consider Arabic numerals that appear in a statement in a specific language or script to be included in the statement. For a manifestation that is published or produced in more than one unit, a statement that appears in the manifestation may describe one or more of the sub-units as well as the manifestation as a unit. For a manifestation that has a super-unit, a statement that appears in the manifestation may describe the super-unit as well as the manifestation as a unit. For a manifestation that embodies the expression of an issue of a diachronic work, a statement that describes the manifestation that embodies the expression of the diachronic work as a super-unit may vary from similar statements that appear in manifestations that embody expressions of previous issues. For a manifestation that embodies content that is not spoken word, tactile text, or text, and if no distinct statement appears in the manifestation, consider text that is embedded in the content as a statement. For a manifestation that embodies performed music, sounds, spoken word, performed movement, or two-dimensional moving image content, statements may be separated from the content or be superimposed on the content. Consider statements of the same type that appear in succession as multiple distinct statements or as components of a single statement. If no unmodified item that exemplifies an older printed sheet or volume is available, consider an imperfect item to be an error in publication. See also: has note on manifestation statement Element values​ The values of this element may be indexed for uncontrolled keywords to support the user task to find the manifestation. Stipulations​ ✽ If one or more statements appear in the manifestation in a script that can be transcribed by the cataloguing agency, record at least one occurrence of the element. Use the following order of preference to select the value: Statement of title and responsibility Statement of publication, production, manufacture, or distribution Statement of issue or iteration Statement of identifier and terms of availability Statement of edition Statement of specific category If a statement appears in a script that cannot be transcribed by the cataloguing agency, record a has note on manifestation statement element or element sub-type that gives a transliteration of the statement in a script of choice of the cataloguing agency, including identification of the script that appears in the manifestation. Examples Property Value has note on manifestation statement of title and responsibility "Transliteracija s kurzivne glagoljice na prednjem omotu: Mrtvi pisani unutra, Žman." [Full example: Mrtvi pisani unutra, Žman ​(1607-1612; Radinić, Pavao, 1549-1611; svezak). The value includes a transliteration from a script that cannot be transcribed by the cataloguing agency.] Apply the General stipulations for statement elements. Examples Property Value has manifestation statement "This catalogue is published in conjunction with the exhibition Matisse – Bonnard. “Long Live Painting!”, Städel Museum, Frankfurt am Main, 13 September 2017 – 14 January 2018" [Full example: Matisse Bonnard ​(2017; Städel Museum; volume).] has manifestation statement "Pete Townshend, Who I am" [The value is a statement of title and responsibility.] has manifestation statement "First published by HarperCollinsPublishers 2012" [The value is a statement of publication, production, manufacture, or distribution.] has manifestation statement "HarperCollinsPublishers … London" [The value is a statement of publication, production, manufacture, or distribution.] has manifestation statement "HP ISBN 978-0-00-746603-0, TPB ISBN 978-0-00-746604-7, EB ISBN 978-0-00-746687-0" [The value is a statement of identifier and terms of availability.] [Full example: Who I am (2012; HarperCollinsPublishers; volume; case binding).] Property Value has manifestation statement "80-рiччю Нацiональноï академiï наук Украïни та Нацiональноï бiблiотеки Украïнi iменi В.I. Веренадського присвячуэться" [Full example: Видатнi вченi Нацiональноï академiï наук Украïнi ​(1998; Нацiональна бiблiотека Украïнi iменi В.I. Веренадського; том).] Use an appropriate element sub-type to record a more specific manifestation statement. Examples Property Value has manifestation statement of title and responsibility "Editor, Ying Ding, Paul Groth, Founding Editor Emeritus, James Hendler" [Full example: Synthesis lectures on data, semantics, and knowledge ​(2021-; Morgan & Claypool Publishers; volume). The value is a statement of responsibility.] Property Value has manifestation statement of publication, production, manufacture, or distribution "First published in Great Britain … 2023" [Full example: In a flight of starlings ​(2023; Allen Lane; volume). The value is a statement of publication.] Property Value has manifestation statement of issue or iteration "Uniwersytet im. Adama Mickiewicza w Poznaniu, Seria Historia Sztuki, NR 27" [Full example: Pałac papieski na Watykanie od końca V do początku XVI wieku ​(1999; Wydawnictwo Naukowe Uniwersytetu im. Adama Mickiewicza; wolumin). The value is a statement of issue of a diachronic work.] Property Value has manifestation statement of identifier and terms of availability "ISBN 0 416 59680 0" [Full example: House at Pooh Corner ​(1986; Methuen Children’s Books; volume). The value is a statement of identifier.] Do not record any value if the manifestation does not make any statements about any aspects of itself. Transcribe a statement that appears in the manifestation. Apply the Rules for transcribing a manifestation statement. Record a separate occurrence of the element for each script in which a statement appears. Avoid mixing different scripts in a single element and omit parts of a statement that are in a different script. Record a separate occurrence of the element for each language in which a statement appears, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Omit parts of a statement that are in a different language. Transcribe a statement that is a pious invocation, a device, an epigram, a dedication, a motto, a statement of patronage or award, or similar, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Transcribe a statement that is known to be inaccurate as it appears on the manifestation. An inaccurate statement may be the result of an error in publication or production, an innocent mistake, or a deliberate intention to conceal information or misrepresent the manifestation. Examples Property Value has manifestation statement "Looser takes all" [Misprint of "Loser takes all".] Property Value has manifestation statement "Chansons créés et interprétés" Transcribe a statement that is known to be fictitious as it appears on the manifestation. For a manifestation that embodies performed music, sounds, spoken word, performed movement, or two-dimensional moving image content, transcribe a statement that appears in succession as a single statement, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Add punctuation to indicate successive components. Do not add a punctuation mark that is the same as one that is transcribed in the statement. Record a has note on manifestation statement element or element sub-type that gives the following kinds of information, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata: A correction to inaccurate or fictitious information that appears in the value of a statement. An expansion of an abbreviation or initialism that appears in the value of a statement. An indication of a conjectural expansion of an abbreviation or initialism that appears in the value of a statement of a manifestation that is an older printed sheet or volume. An explanation or description of the symbol or sign that is replaced in the value of a statement. An explanation or description of a symbol or sign that is omitted in the value of a statement. An explanation or description of a character, word, or ideograph that is intentionally left blank in a statement. An explanation or description of a character, ideograph, or punctuation mark that appears inverted or turned in a statement.

Attribute:Value JSON-LD Turtle RDF/XML Definition Relates a manifestation to a manifestation statement that indicates that the manifestation is a version of another manifestation, and the names, functions, and other details of agents who are responsible for the creation of works and expressions that are embodied in the version. Scope note This element includes editions and drafts, presentation and layout versions, and stages in the manufacture of another manifestation. Attribute:Value JSON-LD Turtle RDF/XML Definition Relates a manifestation to a statement that includes identifiers of the manifestation and general information about obtaining items that exemplify the manifestation. Scope note This element includes identifiers such as key titles, standard numbers, catalogue numbers, plate numbers, and chronological and numeric designations. Terms of availability include limitations on the number of exemplars, the cost, or an indication that there is no cost, of purchasing or borrowing an exemplar, and the categories of agent to whom the terms apply. [Full example: Stax uncovered! ​(2023; H Bauer Publishing Ltd; audio disc).] Record the identifier as it appears in the manifestation, including embedded spaces and punctuation marks. Examples Property Value has manifestation statement of identifier and terms of availability "ISBN 953-222-077-1" [Full example: Hakerska etika i duh informacijskog doba ​(2002; Naklada Jesenski i Turk; svezak).] Property Value has manifestation statement of identifier and terms of availability "ISSN 2813-2696" [Full example: myScience Canada ​(2008-; Scimetrica; online resource).] Record a value that includes a qualifier to an identifier. Examples Property Value has manifestation statement of identifier and terms of availability "HB ISBN 978-1-4087-0515-5" Record a value that includes more than one identifier or terms of availability that are included in a single statement that appears in the manifestation. Examples Property Value has manifestation statement of identifier and terms of availability "ISBN 978-1-78330-185-6 (paperback), ISBN 978-1-78330-186-7 (hardback), ISBN 978-1-783-250-5 (e-book)" [Full example: Open licensing for cultural heritage ​(2017; Facet Publishing; volume; perfect binding).] Record a value that includes a statement about the limited availability of items that exemplify the manifestation, including small numbers of items and restrictions on distribution. Examples Property Value has manifestation statement of identifier and terms of availability "Il a été tiré 15 exemplaires sur alfa cellunaf numéroté de 1 a 15 dont 5 hors commerce constituant l'édition originale" [Full example: Incendie ​(1954; Éditions du Seuil; volume; livre broché).] For a manifestation that embodies performed music, sounds, spoken word, performed movement, or two-dimensional moving image content, record a value that includes a label name that is associated with the catalogue number. Examples Property Value has manifestation statement of identifier and terms of availability "AMMP CD0209" If intermediary identifiers can be inferred, record a value that omits intermediary identifiers from a set of sequentially numbered identifiers. Examples Property Value has manifestation statement of identifier and terms of availability "ART220BD/1 … 8" Property Value has manifestation statement of identifier and terms of availability "8 disks are numbered sequentially."

Attribute:Value JSON-LD Turtle RDF/XML Definition Relates a manifestation to a manifestation statement that includes dates and places of publication, production, manufacture, or distribution of the manifestation, and the names and functions of agents who are responsible for publication, production, manufacture, or distribution of the manifestation. Scope note This element includes roles of agents who are involved in any aspect of the creation and distribution of a manifestation. Creation roles include printing and other forms of mechanical reproduction. Distribution roles include bookselling and other forms of product retail. This element includes statements of copyright, license, or privilege. Examples Property Value has manifestation statement of publication, production, manufacture, or distribution "Дечја књига, Издавачко предузеће НР Србиjе, Београд, 1952" [Full example: Кућа на Пуовом углу ​(1952; Дечја књига; свеска; картон).] Property Value has manifestation statement of publication, production, manufacture, or distribution "... الشركة الوطنية للنشر والتوزيع ... الجزائر، دار الشروق بيروت ... " [Full example: كليلة ودمنة ​(1973؛ الشركة الوطنية للنشر والتوزيع؛ مجلد؛ غلاف مقوى).] Property Value has manifestation statement of publication, production, manufacture, or distribution "Penguin Books Ltd, Harmondsworth … England, … Reprinted 1971" [Full example: Emma ​(1971; Penguin Books; volume).] Record a single occurrence of the element that is selected from one or more values that are associated with the manifestation. Use the following order of preference: A statement about the publication of the manifestation. A statement about the production of the manifestation. A statement about the manufacture of the manifestation. A statement about the distribution of the manifestation. Record additional occurrences of the element, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Examples Property Value has manifestation statement of publication, production, manufacture, or distribution "Facet Publishing" has manifestation statement of publication, production, manufacture, or distribution "Published by Facet Publishing … London …" has manifestation statement of publication, production, manufacture, or distribution "First published 2017" [Full example: Open licensing for cultural heritage ​(2017; Facet Publishing; volume; perfect binding). The value of the most prominent statement does not include a place or date of publication.] Include information about only one of the aspects of publication, production, manufacture, and distribution if more than one aspect is covered by the statement in the manifestation. Use the same order of preference. Include a name, place, and time-span that is associated with an agent who is responsible for publication, production, manufacture, or distribution of the manifestation. Agents​ Include a name that is associated in a manifestation statement with an agent who is responsible for publication, production, manufacture, or distribution of the manifestation. Places​ Include a place that is associated in a manifestation statement with an agent who is responsible for publication, production, manufacture, or distribution of the manifestation. Include a place that is selected from more than one place that is associated with a single instance of an agent in a manifestation statement using the following order of preference: A place that is made more prominent by typography. The first place that appears in the statement. Places that are considered to be useful for users of the metadata. All places. Include an address of a publisher, producer, manufacturer, or distributor, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Include a name of a larger place of publication, production, manufacture, or distribution such as a country, state, etc., if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Time-spans​ Include a date that is associated in a manifestation statement with the publication, production, manufacture, or distribution of the manifestation. Include all dates of publication, production, manufacture, or distribution in different calendars that appear in a manifestation. Include the year of date of publication, production, manufacture, or distribution. Include finer levels of date of publication, production, manufacture, or distribution such as day and month, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Include a statement of date of copyright when it is different from the date of publication, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Include a statement of the latest date of copyright if more than one date of copyright appears in the manifestation.

Record a value that appears in the manifestation. Do not record a value that does not appear in the manifestation. If more than one statement is associated with the same aspect of the manifestation, record a separate occurrence of the element for each distinct statement that is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Use the following order of preference: The prominence of statements that appear in the manifestation. The fullness of statements within the scope of the element. The utility of statements for users of the metadata. The order of statements that appear in the manifestation. If a statement is duplicated in different languages or scripts, record a separate occurrence of the element for each distinct statement that is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Use the following order of preference: The languages and scripts that are preferred by the cataloguing agency. The order of statements that appear in the manifestation. For a manifestation that embodies the expression of a diachronic work, record a value that describes only the manifestation. Omit a statement or part of a statement that describes a manifestation that embodies an expression of an issue of the work. For a manifestation that embodies the expression of a diachronic work, and if there is a change in the information that is given in statements that describe the manifestation and appear in manifestations that embody expressions of issues or iterations of the work, record an additional occurrence of the element for the statement that has changed, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. For a manifestation that embodies an expression of an issue of a diachronic work, record only a value that describes the manifestation. Record a statement or part of a statement that describes the manifestation of the expression of the diachronic work as a value of a has manifestation statement of issue or iteration element.
documents.s: General stipulations for manifestation statement elements

documents.t: ISBD for Manifestation encourages the use of controlled terminology for a value of an attribute or relationship element: ISBDM prescribes the use of a controlled term as a value of a specified attribute element. ISBDM suggests a string encoding scheme (SES) to construct a value of a relationship element or a specified attribute element. A value vocabulary contains a set of controlled terms that are used as values for a specific ISBDM attribute element. A value vocabulary is also known as a vocabulary encoding scheme (VES). Prescribed vocabularies for specific elements are listed in the top part of the section menu. Record a plural form of a controlled term where appropriate. A string encoding scheme specifies the elements, fixed text, and punctuation that are used to construct an access point or structured string as the value of an element. General guidance on string encoding schemes is included with the appropriate elements. Suggested schemes for specific elements are listed in the bottom part of the section menu. See also: ISBDM string encoding schemes.

Transcribe a manifestation statement in the orthography and grammatical case in which it appears in the manifestation. Amend the case of letters in a bicameral script to the orthography of the language, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Transcribe a character, ideograph, or punctuation mark in its correct orientation if it is inverted or turned in a statement by mistake or deliberate act. Consider an abbreviation that consists of more than one letter to be a distinct word. Consider a set of initials or an acronym to be an initialism or distinct word. Omit spaces within an initialism. Include words and phrases that are considered to be useful for identifying the manifestation, its attributes, and its relationships to other entities. Include words and phrases that are grammatically linked to an instance of an entity in the statement. These include prepositions, articles, and conjunctions. Include honorifics and other terms of address that are associated with a name of a person in a manifestation statement, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Include references to more than one instance of an entity in the statement in the order of their appearance in the statement. Repeat a word or phrase that is intended through typography and layout to be read twice or to be associated with more than one statement. Do not abbreviate or expand words that appear as full forms or abbreviations respectively in the manifestation. Replace indentation, new lines, and other whitespace within a statement with a single space. Add punctuation to improve clarity, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Do not add a punctuation mark that is the same as one that is transcribed. Replace an earlier form of a letter or symbol with a modern equivalent. Replace a ligature with its component characters, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Replace quotation marks within a statement with encoded quotation marks that are distinct from quotation marks that are used to delimit a value that is a literal string. Replace a symbol or sign that cannot be reproduced by the facilities available to the cataloguing agency with an equivalent character. Replace a rebus with the word that it represents in the language or script of the statement. Replace an image that appears within a statement with a word or phrase that it represents in the language or script of the statement. Do not amend the capitalization of words or phrases that contain a chronogram. Omit words and phrases from a manifestation statement for any of the following reasons: The text is insignificant to identify or find the manifestation The text is included in another manifestation statement unless it is grammatically linked to the instance transcribed. The statement is lengthy and truncation does not impair support for the user task to identify the manifestation. Omit words, abbreviations, or initials in a name or title that are duplicated in a fuller or shorter form within the same statement, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. Omit a symbol or sign that cannot be reproduced by the facilities available to the cataloguing agency. Use an ellipsis to indicate where content is omitted from within the manifestation statement during transcription. An ellipsis is the "mark of omission" consisting of three dots or full-stops (…).
documents.s: Rules for transcribing a manifestation statement

documents.t: For use with element: has category of carrier This value vocabulary is a source of values for a has category of carrier element. The vocabulary covers the full scope of the element and will not be extended with additional values. Value Definition Scope note aperture card (isbdm:1022#t1000) A carrier type that consists of a card with one or more rectangular openings or apertures holding frames of microfilm. audio belt (isbdm:1022#t1001) A carrier type that consists of a loop of flexible plastic or magnetic film on which audio signals are mechanically recorded, commonly known under the trade name Dictabelt. audio cartridge (isbdm:1022#t1002) A carrier type that consists of a cartridge containing an audio tape. audio cylinder (isbdm:1022#t1003) A carrier type that consists of a roller-shaped object on which sound waves are incised or indented in a continuous circular groove. Wax cylinders, wire cylinders, etc., are included. audio disc (isbdm:1022#t1004) A carrier type that consists of a disc on which sound waves, recorded as modulations, pulses, etc., are incised or indented in a continuous spiral groove. audio roll (isbdm:1022#t1005) A carrier type that consists of a roll of paper on which musical notes are represented by perforations, designed to mechanically reproduce the music when used in a player piano, player organ, etc. audio wire reel (isbdm:1022#t1006) A carrier type that consists of a reel or spool of steel or stainless steel wire upon which audio signals are magnetically recorded. audiocassette (isbdm:1022#t1007) A carrier type that consists of a cassette containing an audiotape. audiotape reel (isbdm:1022#t1008) A carrier type that consists of an open reel holding a length of audiotape to be used with reel-to-reel audio equipment. card (isbdm:1022#t1009) A carrier type that consists of a small sheet of opaque material. computer card (isbdm:1022#t1010) A carrier type that consists of a card containing digitally encoded data designed for use with a computer. computer chip cartridge (isbdm:1022#t1011) A carrier type that consists of a cartridge containing a miniaturized electronic circuit on a small wafer of semiconductor silicon, designed to provide additional processing, memory, or storage capacity. computer disc (isbdm:1022#t1012) A carrier type that consists of a disc containing digitally encoded data that are magnetically or optically recorded. computer disc cartridge (isbdm:1022#t1013) A carrier type that consists of a cartridge containing one or more computer discs. computer tape cartridge (isbdm:1022#t1014) A carrier type that consists of a cartridge containing a computer tape. computer tape cassette (isbdm:1022#t1015) A carrier type that consists of a cassette containing a computer tape. computer tape reel (isbdm:1022#t1016) A carrier type that consists of an open reel holding a length of computer tape to be used with a computer tape drive. film cartridge (isbdm:1022#t1017) A carrier type that consists of a cartridge containing a motion picture film. film cassette (isbdm:1022#t1018) A carrier type that consists of a cassette containing a motion picture film. film reel (isbdm:1022#t1019) A carrier type that consists of an open reel holding a motion picture film to be used with a motion picture film projector. film roll (isbdm:1022#t1020) A carrier type that consists of a wound length of film. filmslip (isbdm:1022#t1021) A carrier type that consists of a short strip of film, usually in rigid format rather than rolled. filmstrip (isbdm:1022#t1022) A carrier type that consists of a roll of film, with or without recorded sound, containing a succession of images intended for projection one at a time. filmstrip cartridge (isbdm:1022#t1023) A carrier type that consists of a cartridge containing a filmstrip. flipchart (isbdm:1022#t1024) A carrier type that consists of a hinging device holding two or more sheets designed for use on an easel. microfiche (isbdm:1022#t1025) A carrier type that consists of a sheet of film bearing a number of micro-images in a two-dimensional array. microfiche cassette (isbdm:1022#t1026) A carrier type that consists of a cassette containing uncut microfiches. microfilm cartridge (isbdm:1022#t1027) A carrier type that consists of a cartridge containing a microfilm. microfilm cassette (isbdm:1022#t1028) A carrier type that consists of a cassette containing a microfilm. microfilm reel (isbdm:1022#t1029) A carrier type that consists of an open reel holding a microfilm, to be threaded into a microfilm reader. microfilm roll (isbdm:1022#t1030) A carrier type that consists of a wound length of microfilm. microfilm slip (isbdm:1022#t1031) A carrier type that consists of a short strip of microfilm cut from a roll. microopaque (isbdm:1022#t1032) A carrier type that consists of a card or sheet of opaque material bearing a number of micro-images in a two-dimensional array. microscope slide (isbdm:1022#t1033) A carrier type that consists of a small sheet of transparent material, with or without a protective mount, bearing a minute object designed for use with a device such as a microscope. object (isbdm:1022#t1034) A carrier type that consists of a three-dimensional artefact, a replica of an artefact, or a naturally-occurring object. online resource (isbdm:1022#t1035) A carrier type that consists of a digital resource accessed by means of hardware and software connections to a communications network. overhead transparency (isbdm:1022#t1036) A carrier type that consists of a sheet of transparent material, with or without a protective mount, bearing an image designed for use with an overhead projector. roll (isbdm:1022#t1037) A carrier type that consists of a wound length of paper, film, tape, etc. sheet (isbdm:1022#t1038) A carrier type that consists of a flat, thin piece of paper, plastic, etc. slide (isbdm:1022#t1039) A carrier type that consists of a small sheet of transparent material, usually in a protective mount, bearing an image designed for use with a slide projector or viewer. sound-track reel (isbdm:1022#t1040) A carrier type that consists of an open reel holding a length of film on which sound is recorded. Use for sound-track films, whether or not they are intended to accompany visual images on film. stereograph card (isbdm:1022#t1041) A carrier type that consists of a card bearing stereographic images. stereograph disc (isbdm:1022#t1042) A carrier type that consists of a disc with openings around the perimeter holding pairs of still images designed for use with a stereograph viewer. video cartridge (isbdm:1022#t1043) A carrier type that consists of a cartridge containing a video tape. videocassette (isbdm:1022#t1044) A carrier type that consists of a cassette containing a video tape. videodisc (isbdm:1022#t1045) A carrier type that consists of a disc on which video signals, with or without sound, are recorded. videotape reel (isbdm:1022#t1046) A carrier type that consists of an open reel holding a video tape for use with reel-to-reel video equipment. volume (isbdm:1022#t1047) A carrier type that consists of one or more sheets bound or fastened together to form a single unit.
