documents.t: For use with element: has media type This value vocabulary is a source of values for a has media type element. The vocabulary covers the full scope of the element and will not be extended with additional values. Value Definition Scope note audio (isbdm:1218#t1000) A media type used to store recorded sound, designed for use with a playback device such as a turntable, audiocassette player, CD player, or MP3 player. Media used to store digitally encoded as well as analog sound are included. computer (isbdm:1218#t1001) A media type used to store electronic files, designed for use with a computer. Media that are accessed remotely through file servers as well as direct-access media such as computer tapes and discs are included. microform (isbdm:1218#t1002) A media type used to store reduced-size images not readable to the human eye, designed for use with a device such as a microfilm or microfiche reader. Both transparent and opaque micrographic media are included. microscopic (isbdm:1218#t1003) A media type used to store minute objects, designed for use with a device such as a microscope to reveal details invisible to the naked eye. projected (isbdm:1218#t1004) A media type used to store moving or still images, designed for use with a projection device such as a motion picture film projector, slide projector, or overhead projector. Media designed to project both two-dimensional and three-dimensional images are included. stereographic (isbdm:1218#t1005) A media type used to store pairs of still images, designed for use with a device such as a stereoscope or stereograph viewer to give the effect of three dimensions. unmediated (isbdm:1218#t1006) A media type used to store content designed to be perceived directly through one or more of the human senses without the aid of an intermediating device. Media containing visual or tactile content produced using processes such as printing, engraving, lithography, etc., embossing, texturing, etc., or by means of handwriting, drawing, painting, etc., are included. Media used to convey three-dimensional forms such as sculptures, models, etc., are also included. video (isbdm:1218#t1007) A media type used to store moving or still images, designed for use with a playback device such as a videocassette player or DVD player. Media used to store digitally encoded as well as analog images are included. The values, definitions, and scope notes in this vocabulary are derived from the RDA Media Type value vocabulary licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License, copyright © 2020 American Library Association, Canadian Federation of Library Associations, and CILIP: Chartered Institute of Library and Information Professionals.

For use with element: has bibliographic format This value vocabulary is a source of values for a has bibliographic format element. The vocabulary covers the full scope of the element and will not be extended with additional values. Value Definition Scope note 4to (isbdm:1240#t1000) A bibliographic format that consists of one or more leaves that are 1/4 of the whole sheet. 8vo (isbdm:1240#t1001) A bibliographic format that consists of one or more leaves that are 1/8 of the whole sheet. 12mo (isbdm:1240#t1002) A bibliographic format that consists of one or more leaves that are 1/12 of the whole sheet. 16mo (isbdm:1240#t1003) A bibliographic format that consists of one or more leaves that are 1/16 of the whole sheet. 18mo (isbdm:1240#t1004) A bibliographic format that consists of one or more leaves that are 1/18 of the whole sheet. 24mo (isbdm:1240#t1005) A bibliographic format that consists of one or more leaves that are 1/24 of the whole sheet. 32mo (isbdm:1240#t1006) A bibliographic format that consists of one or more leaves that are 1/32 of the whole sheet. 48mo (isbdm:1240#t1007) A bibliographic format that consists of one or more leaves that are 1/48 of the whole sheet. 64mo (isbdm:1240#t1008) A bibliographic format that consists of one or more leaves that are 1/64 of the whole sheet. 36mo (isbdm:1240#t1009) A bibliographic format that consists of one or more leaves that are 1/36 of the whole sheet. 72mo (isbdm:1240#t1010) A bibliographic format that consists of one or more leaves that are 1/72 of the whole sheet. 96mo (isbdm:1240#t1011) A bibliographic format that consists of one or more leaves that are 1/96 of the whole sheet. 128mo (isbdm:1240#t1012) A bibliographic format that consists of one or more leaves that are 1/128 of the whole sheet. folio (isbdm:1240#t1013) A bibliographic format that consists of one or more leaves that are 1/2 of the whole sheet. full-sheet (isbdm:1240#t1014) A bibliographic format that consists of one or more sheets that have not been cut or folded. The values, definitions, and scope notes in this vocabulary are derived from the RDA Bibliographic Format value vocabulary licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License, copyright © 2020 American Library Association, Canadian Federation of Library Associations, and CILIP: Chartered Institute of Library and Information Professionals.

For use with element: has binding This value vocabulary is a source of values for a has binding element. The vocabulary does not cover the full scope of the element and may be extended with additional values. Value Definition Scope note board book binding (isbdm:1241#t1000) A type of binding for sheets of thick paperboard with covers that are folded and bound to form a spine. The binding is durable and often used for manifestations for children. Outer covers are of the same thickness of paperboard as the sheets. case binding (isbdm:1241#t1001) A type of binding that sews or glues sheets into sections that are glued together to form a flat spine and that are attached to endpapers which are in turn attached to a stiff outer casing. Sheets may be folded to form gatherings. The outer casing of the volume is usually made of board, wood, plastic, or some other rigid material. closed ring binding (isbdm:1241#t1002) A type of binding that uses two or more rings of metal or plastic that are threaded through holes along the edge of each sheet. The rings are widely spaced and require a spine to maintain the spacing. Outer covers may be attached directly to the spine, or threaded by the rings. comb binding (isbdm:1241#t1003) A type of binding that uses multiple closely-spaced curved flaps of metal or plastic that are threaded through holes along the edge of each sheet. The binding flaps usually form a curved spine. Outer covers are generally threaded by the flaps. dos-a-dos binding (isbdm:1241#t1004) A type of binding that uses two outer casings and an inner casing that is shared between two sets of sheets to form two spines. One spine faces outwards and the other spine faces inwards, depending on how the volume is oriented. open ring binding (isbdm:1241#t1005) A type of binding that uses two or more rings of metal or plastic that are threaded through holes along the edge of each sheet, and that can be opened to allow the removal or insertion of any sheet. The rings are widely spaced and require a spine to maintain the spacing. Outer covers may be attached directly to the spine or threaded by the rings. perfect binding (isbdm:1241#t1006) A type of binding that glues sheets together and to a flexible outer casing to form a spine. Sheets may be folded to form gatherings. The outer casing of the volume is usually made of thin card, plastic, or some other flexible material. saddle stitch binding (isbdm:1241#t1007) A type of binding that folds sheets and staples them along the fold to form a spine. The staples may be made of metal, plastic, or textile. Outer covers made of a flexible material are also folded and stapled to the sheets. slide binding (isbdm:1241#t1008) A type of binding that uses a single length of metal or plastic bent into a C cross-section which slides over the edge of each sheet to hold it in place. Outer covers of the volume may be made of a thin flexible material that can be inserted as a sheet into the binding strip. spiral binding (isbdm:1241#t1009) A type of binding that uses a continuous wire or plastic coil that is threaded through holes along the edge of each sheet. Outer covers of the volume may be made of a rigid or flexible material, and may be attached directly to the coil or threaded by the coil springback binding (isbdm:1241#t1010) A type of binding that clamps the edge of each sheet in a metal spring that is directly attached to a spine and outer covers, and that can be opened to allow the removal or insertion of any sheet.

For use with element: has manufacturing process This value vocabulary is a source of values for a has manufacturing process element. The vocabulary does not cover the full scope of the element and may be extended with additional values. Value Definition Scope note blueline process (isbdm:1256#t1000) A production method that consists of a contact printing process based on diazonium salt and azo dye chemical reactions that renders all opaque tones or colours as blue on a neutral background. blueprint process (isbdm:1256#t1001) A production method that consists of a contact printing process based on iron salt chemical reactions that renders all opaque tones or colours as white on a blue background. burning (isbdm:1256#t1002) A production method that consists of the application of heat to mark the surface of a material. collotype (isbdm:1256#t1003) A production method that consists of a contact printing process using a dichromate chemical reaction that hardens gelatin on exposure to ultraviolet light to produce a positive master that is subsequently used in a lithographic process. daguerreotype process (isbdm:1256#t1004) A production method that consists of a photographic process using a silver-coated copper plate that is exposed in a camera and subsequently developed, usually using mercury vapour, and fixed with salt to create a positive image. embossing (isbdm:1256#t1005) A production method that consists of the use of either a metal or plastic sheet as a master with specialized equipment to produce copies for a manifestation of a tactile expression. engraving (isbdm:1256#t1006) A production method that consists of the incision of marks on the surface of a hard material using a sharp tool. Engraving includes the preparation of a printing plate for an intaglio process. etching (isbdm:1256#t1007) A production method that consists of an intaglio process in which a design is worked into an acid-resistant substance coating a metal printing plate; the plate is then exposed to acid, which etches the plate where the metal is exposed, to create lines and dark areas. inscribing (isbdm:1256#t1008) A production method that consists of a process that fixes signs and symbols onto a base material by cutting into the surface. lithography (isbdm:1256#t1009) A production method that consists of a planographic printing process in which a stone or plate is prepared using a water-repelling substance making parts of the plate receptive to ink. photocopying (isbdm:1256#t1010) A production method that consists of a macroform photoreproduction process using radiant energy in contact with or projected on opaque material. photoengraving (isbdm:1256#t1011) A production method that consists of a photomechanical process for the preparation of chemically etched printing plates. photogravure process (isbdm:1256#t1012) A production method that consists of an intaglio process in which the metal printing plate is prepared using a dichromate process to leave a gelatin resist coating of varying thickness that is etched to form cells of varying depth able to hold different amounts of ink. printing (isbdm:1256#t1013) A production method that consists of a process that transfers a pictorial or textual image from a master carrier to the surface of another carrier, often using a plate, block, stone, or screen coated with a transferable material. Includes the production of photographic prints and paper copies of stored computer data. solid dot (isbdm:1256#t1014) A production method for a manifestation of a tactile expression in which solid plastic dots are heat sealed onto the surface of thin but strong paper. stamping (isbdm:1256#t1015) A production method that consists of the application of pressure to make an impression on the surface of a material. swell paper (isbdm:1256#t1016) A production method for a manifestation of a tactile expression in which an image is printed on a special type of paper with embedded microcapsules of alcohol which burst when exposed to heat to make the surface of the paper swell up. thermoform (isbdm:1256#t1017) A production method for a manifestation of a tactile expression in which a collage master is covered with a sheet of plastic, which is heated and vacuumed to generate a copy of a model or diagram. white print process (isbdm:1256#t1018) A production method that consists of a contact printing process based on a light sensitive process that renders all opaque tones or colours as black or a colour on a white background. woodcut making (isbdm:1256#t1019) A production method that consists of a relief process in which a design is cut into and printed from the surface of a wood block.

For use with element: has unitary structure This value vocabulary is a source of values for a has unitary structure element. The vocabulary covers the full scope of the element and will not be extended with additional values. Value Definition Scope note multiple unit (isbdm:1262#t1000) A unitary structure that is two or more parts. single unit (isbdm:1262#t1001) A unitary structure that is a whole. The values, definitions, and scope notes in this vocabulary are derived from the RDA Mode of Issuance value vocabulary licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License, copyright © 2020 American Library Association, Canadian Federation of Library Associations, and CILIP: Chartered Institute of Library and Information Professionals.

For use with element: has category of embodied content This value vocabulary is a source of values for a has category of embodied content element. The vocabulary covers the full scope of the element and will not be extended with additional values. Value Definition Scope note cartographic dataset (isbdm:1264#t1000) A content type that consists of cartographic content expressed through a digitally encoded dataset intended to be processed by a computer. A cartographic dataset excludes cartographic data intended to be perceived in the form of an image or three-dimensional form. cartographic image (isbdm:1264#t1001) A content type that consists of cartographic content expressed through line, shape, shading, etc., intended to be perceived visually as a still image or images in two dimensions. Maps, views, atlases, remote-sensing images, etc., are included. cartographic moving image (isbdm:1264#t1002) A content type that consists of cartographic content expressed through images intended to be perceived as moving, in two dimensions. Satellite images of the earth or other celestial bodies in motion are included. cartographic tactile image (isbdm:1264#t1003) A content type that consists of cartographic content expressed through line, shape, and/or other forms, intended to be perceived through touch as a still image in two dimensions. cartographic tactile three-dimensional form (isbdm:1264#t1004) A content type that consists of cartographic content expressed through a form or forms intended to be perceived through touch as a three-dimensional form or forms. cartographic three-dimensional form (isbdm:1264#t1005) A content type that consists of cartographic content expressed through a form or forms intended to be perceived visually in three-dimensions. Globes, relief models, etc., are included. computer dataset (isbdm:1264#t1006) A content type that consists of content expressed through a digitally encoded dataset intended to be processed by a computer. Numeric data, environmental data, etc., used by applications software to calculate averages, correlations, etc., or to produce models, etc., but not normally displayed in its raw form, are included. Excludes data intended to be perceived visually in the form of notation, image, or three-dimensional form. For data intended to be perceived in an audible form, see performed music, sounds, and spoken word. For cartographic data, see cartographic dataset. computer program (isbdm:1264#t1007) A content type that consists of content expressed through digitally encoded instructions intended to be processed and performed by a computer. Operating systems, applications software, etc., are included. notated movement (isbdm:1264#t1008) A content type that consists of content expressed through a form of notation for movement intended to be perceived visually. All forms of movement notation other than those intended to be perceived through touch are included. notated music (isbdm:1264#t1009) A content type that consists of content expressed through a form of musical notation intended to be perceived visually. All forms of music notation other than those intended to be perceived through touch are included. performed movement (isbdm:1264#t1010) A content type that consists of content expressed through choreography in a visual form. Includes performed dance and mime, and animated choreography. performed music (isbdm:1264#t1011) A content type that consists of content expressed through music in an audible form. Recorded performances of music, computer-generated music, etc., are included. sounds (isbdm:1264#t1012) A content type that consists of content other than language or music, expressed in an audible form. Natural sounds, artificially produced sounds, etc., are included. spoken word (isbdm:1264#t1013) A content type that consists of content expressed through language in an audible form. Recorded readings, recitations, speeches, interviews, oral histories, etc., computer-generated speech, etc., are included. still image (isbdm:1264#t1014) A content type that consists of content expressed through line, shape, shading, etc., intended to be perceived visually as a still image or images in two dimensions. Drawings, paintings, diagrams, photographic images known as stills, etc., are included. For cartographic content intended to be perceived as a two-dimensional image, see cartographic image. For images intended to be perceived through touch, see tactile image. tactile image (isbdm:1264#t1015) A content type that consists of content expressed through line, shape, and/or other forms, intended to be perceived through touch as a still image in two dimensions. tactile notated music (isbdm:1264#t1016) A content type that consists of content expressed through a form of musical notation intended to be perceived through touch. Braille music and other tactile forms of musical notation are included. tactile notated movement (isbdm:1264#t1017) A content type that consists of content expressed through a form of notation for movement intended to be perceived through touch. tactile text (isbdm:1264#t1018) A content type that consists of content expressed through a form of notation for language intended to be perceived through touch. Braille text and other tactile forms of language notation are included. tactile three-dimensional form (isbdm:1264#t1019) A content type that consists of content expressed through a form or forms intended to be perceived through touch as a three-dimensional form or forms. text (isbdm:1264#t1020) A content type that consists of content expressed through a form of notation for language intended to be perceived visually. All forms of language notation other than those intended to be perceived through touch are included. three-dimensional form (isbdm:1264#t1021) A content type that consists of content expressed through a form or forms intended to be perceived visually in three-dimensions. Sculptures, models, naturally occurring objects and specimens, holograms, etc., are included. Excludes cartographic content intended to be perceived as a three-dimensional form. Excludes three-dimensional forms intended to be perceived through touch. three-dimensional moving image (isbdm:1264#t1022) A content type that consists of content expressed through images intended to be perceived to be moving, and in three dimensions. Three-dimensional motion pictures using live action or animation, and stereoscopic, known as S-3D, video games, etc., are included. Three-dimensional moving images may or may not be accompanied by sound. two-dimensional moving image (isbdm:1264#t1023) A content type that consists of content expressed through images intended to be perceived to be moving, and in two dimensions. Motion pictures using live action and/or animation, film and video recordings of performances, events, etc., other than those intended to be perceived in three dimensions, are included. Moving images may or may not be accompanied by sound. The values, definitions, and scope notes in this vocabulary are derived from the RDA Content Type value vocabulary licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License, copyright © 2020 American Library Association, Canadian Federation of Library Associations, and CILIP: Chartered Institute of Library and Information Professionals.

documents.t: For use with element: has extent of unitary structure This value vocabulary is a source of values for a has extent of unitary structure element. The vocabulary does not cover the full scope of the element and may be extended with additional values. Value Definition Scope note activity card (isbdm:1275#t1000) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is a card to be used as a basis for performing a specific activity. An activity card may be part of a set of cards, and usually embodies a text or a still image. coin (isbdm:1275#t1001) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is an object that is a piece of metal stamped by government authority for use as money. collage (isbdm:1275#t1002) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is a sheet on which is affixed paper, textiles, or other two-dimensional materials. A collage usually embodies a still image. diorama (isbdm:1275#t1003) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is an object in which miniature scenery, figurines, and other components are placed in front of a background sheet to embody a three-dimensional form. exhibit (isbdm:1275#t1004) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is an object ithat consists of other objects gathered together for display. An exhibit may include display cases, captions, and panels that give information about the gathered objects. flash card (isbdm:1275#t1005) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is a card that is used for rapid display as an aid to learning. game (isbdm:1275#t1006) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is an object that consists of a group of other objects that are manipulated according to a set of rules for purposes of education, entertainment, or therapy. globe (isbdm:1275#t1007) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is an object that is a sphere. A globe embodies a cartographic image on its surface. jigsaw puzzle (isbdm:1275#t1008) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is a sheet that is cut into interlocking shapes for reassembly. A jigsaw puzzle usually embodies a still image. medal (isbdm:1275#t1009) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is an object that is a piece of metal that is used to commemorate something. mock-up (isbdm:1275#t1010) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is an object that is a scaled-down representation of a part of another object that may be modified for training or analysis to emphasize a particular part or function. model (isbdm:1275#t1011) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is an object that is a scaled-down representation of another object. painting (isbdm:1275#t1012) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is a sheet on which pigment is applied by hand. A painting embodies a still image. piece (isbdm:1275#t1013) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is a sheet or object that is intended for manipulation as a component of a game or puzzle. postcard (isbdm:1275#t1014) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is a card that is used for sending a message without an envelope via a mail service. A postcard may embody a text or a still image. poster (isbdm:1275#t1015) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is a sheet that is used to publicize an event, product, or service, or as a decorative wall hanging. A poster may embody a text or a still image print (isbdm:1275#t1016) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is a sheet that is used for a high-quality reproduction. A print embodies a still image. sculpture (isbdm:1275#t1017) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is an object made of material that is worked into a shape. A sculpture embodies a three-dimensional image. specimen (isbdm:1275#t1018) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is an object tthat is intended to be representative of a larger group of similar objects. study print (isbdm:1275#t1019) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is a sheet that is used for education. A study print embodies a still image that may be augmented with a text. toy (isbdm:1275#t1020) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is an object that is intended for education, entertainment, or stimulation through play. wall chart (isbdm:1275#t1021) A unit of extent of unitary structure that is a sheet that is intended for display on a wall.
documents.s: ISBDM Extent of Unitary Structure value vocabulary

documents.t: For use with element: has extent of aggregated content This value vocabulary is a source of values for a has extent of aggregated content element. The vocabulary does not cover the full scope of the element and may be extended with additional values. Value Definition Scope note chart (isbdm:1278#t1000) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is a still image that is a representation of data in graphic or tabular form. diagram (isbdm:1278#t1001) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is a still image that is a representation of numeric data, or of an action or process. drawing (isbdm:1278#t1002) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is a still image that is composed of lines that represent the delineation of form. icon (isbdm:1278#t1003) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is a still image that portrays a sacred entity and that is itself regarded as sacred. map (isbdm:1278#t1004) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is a cartographic image that represents an area on the surface of the earth, another celestial body, or an imaginary place. part (isbdm:1278#t1005) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is notated music. performed dance (isbdm:1278#t1006) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is performed movement that is recorded in a live performance. performed song (isbdm:1278#t1007) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is performed music that is recorded in a live performance. photograph (isbdm:1278#t1008) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is a still image that is captured by a lens. profile (isbdm:1278#t1009) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is a cartographic image. radiograph (isbdm:1278#t1010) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is a still image produced by radiation. recorded song (isbdm:1278#t1011) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is performed music that is recorded in a studio. remote-sensing image (isbdm:1278#t1012) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is a cartographic image that is captured by a remote-sensing instrument. score (isbdm:1278#t1013) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is notated music. section (isbdm:1278#t1014) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is a cartographic image that represents a slice through the surface of the earth or some other celestial body. spoken text (isbdm:1278#t1015) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is spoken word that is a recitation of a text. technical drawing (isbdm:1278#t1016) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is a still image that represents a cross section of an object or part of an object for use in an engineering or other technical context. view (isbdm:1278#t1017) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is a still image that represents a landscape from an oblique point of view. A bird's-eye view, panorama, panoramic drawing, worm's-eye view, etc., are included. vocal score (isbdm:1278#t1018) A unit of extent of aggregated content that is notated music.
documents.s: ISBDM Extent of Aggregated Content value vocabulary

documents.t: For use with element: has regional encoding This value vocabulary is a source of values for a has regional encoding element. The vocabulary does not cover the full scope of the element and may be extended with additional values. Value Definition Scope note all regions (isbdm:1283#t1000) A regional encoding for a videodisc or video game carrier that indicates that playback is permitted on devices worldwide. Region 1 (isbdm:1283#t1001) A regional encoding for a DVD videodisc encoded for playback by devices configured to decode it in the United States, Canada, Bermuda, and U.S. territories. Region 2 (isbdm:1283#t1002) A regional encoding for a DVD videodisc encoded for playback by devices configured to decode it in Japan, Europe, South Africa, and the Middle East, including Egypt. Region 3 (isbdm:1283#t1003) A regional encoding for a DVD videodisc encoded for playback by devices configured to decode it in Southeast Asia and East Asia, including Hong Kong. Region 4 (isbdm:1283#t1004) A regional encoding for a DVD videodisc encoded for playback by devices configured to decode it in Australia, New Zealand, Pacific Islands, Central America, South America, and the Caribbean. Region 5 (isbdm:1283#t1005) A regional encoding for a DVD videodisc encoded for playback by devices configured to decode it in Eastern Europe, Baltic States, Russia, Central and South Asia, Indian subcontinent, Africa, North Korea, and Mongolia. Region 6 (isbdm:1283#t1006) A regional encoding for a DVD videodisc encoded for playback by devices configured to decode it in China. Region 7 (isbdm:1283#t1007) A regional encoding for a DVD videodisc encoded for playback by devices configured to decode it for special uses, such as playing protected copies sent to film industry professionals or to the media. Region 8 (isbdm:1283#t1008) A regional encoding for a DVD videodisc encoded for playback by devices configured to decode it in international venues such as aircraft, cruise ships, spacecraft, etc. Region A (isbdm:1283#t1009) A regional encoding for a Blu-ray videodisc encoded for playback by devices configured to decode it in North America, Central America, South America, Japan, North Korea, South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Southeast Asia. Region B (isbdm:1283#t1010) A regional encoding for a Blu-ray videodisc encoded for playback by devices configured to decode it in Europe, Greenland, French territories, Middle East, Africa, Australia, and New Zealand. Region C (Blu-ray) (isbdm:1283#t1011) A regional encoding for a Blu-ray videodisc encoded for playback by devices configured to decode it in India, Nepal, mainland China, Russia, Central Asia, and South Asia. Region C (video game) (isbdm:1283#t1012) A regional encoding for a video game carrier encoded for playback by devices configured to decode it in China. Region J (isbdm:1283#t1013) A regional encoding for a video game carrier encoded for playback by devices configured to decode it in Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau, and Southeast Asia. Region U/C (isbdm:1283#t1014) A regional encoding for a video game carrier encoded for playback by devices configured to decode it in the United States, Canada, Mexico, and South America. The values, definitions, and scope notes in this vocabulary are derived from the RDA Regional Encoding value vocabulary licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License, copyright © 2020 American Library Association, Canadian Federation of Library Associations, and CILIP: Chartered Institute of Library and Information Professionals.

For use with element: has layout of embodied content This value vocabulary is a source of values for a has layout of embodied content element. The vocabulary does not cover the full scope of the element and may be extended with additional values. Value Definition Scope note columns (isbdm:1288#t1000) A layout of embodied content where content is arranged in two or more vertical sections on a page, separated by vertical gutters. This value applies to a manifestation that is a card, sheet, or volume. frames (isbdm:1288#t1001) A layout of embodied content where content is arranged in two or more blockes on a page, separated by horizontal or vertical gutters. This value applies to a manifestation that is an aperture card, card, film roll, filmslip, filmstrip, filmstrip cartridge, microfiche, microfiche cassette, microfilm cartridge, microfilm cassette, microfilm reel, microfilm roll, microfilm slip, microopaque, sheet, stereograph disc, or volume. pages (isbdm:1288#t1002) A layout of embodied content where content is embodied in both sides of a leaf or sheet. This value applies to a manifestation that is a card, sheet, or volume. tête-bêche (isbdm:1288#t1003) A layout of embodied content that is two sets of content embodied in a volume where the sets are rotated 180° relative to each other so that one set is accessed from the front of the binding and the other from the back. This value applies to a manifestation that is a volume.
documents.s: ISBDM Layout of Embodied Content value vocabulary

documents.t: For use with element: has designation of number of sound channels This value vocabulary is a source of values for a has designation of number of sound channels element. The vocabulary covers the full scope of the element and will not be extended with additional values. Value Definition Scope note mono (isbdm:1285#t1000) A designation of sound channels that is a single channel for monophonic sound. quadraphonic (isbdm:1285#t1001) A designation of sound channels that is four channels for quadraphonic sound. stereo (isbdm:1285#t1002) A designation of sound channels that is two channels for stereophonic sound. surround (isbdm:1285#t1003) A designation of sound channels that is more than four channels for surround sound. documents.t: ISBD for Manifestation does not prescribe a selection, order, layout, or punctuation for displaying the values of elements in a description of a manifestation. The choice of methods for displaying ISBDM metadata in an information retrieval application is influenced by the intended Metadata utility and processing of ISBDM elements. The value of a has manifestation statement element or element sub-type is at a broad level of granularity, and it may overlap with the value of another similar element. Specific element labels may be omitted to simplify the display of a set of values. Examples Relation Example display of ISBDM metadata ""Jane Austen, Emma, edited with an introduction by Ronald Blythe. - Penguin English library. - Penguin Books Ltd, Harmondsworth … England, … Reprinted 1971. - ISBN 0 14 043.101 5."" [Full example: Emma ​(1971; Penguin Books; volume). The delimiting punctuation is ". - " (stop-space-hyphen-space).] Relation Example display of ISBDM metadata ""give it up b/w tired. - lcd soundsystem [Full example: Give it up b/w Tired ​(2002; Ouput Recordings; audio disc). The delimiting punctuation is ". - " (stop-space-hyphen-space).] Relation Example display of ISBDM metadata ""Henri Cartier-Bresson (1908-2004) / Truman Capote, ecrivain, USA, 1947 / courtesy Fondation HCB : © Nouvelles Images S.A. et H. Cartier-Bresson - Magnum Photos 2008 / 45700 Lombreuil, France : 764697001022, 764697150065"" [Full example: Truman Capote, ecrivain, USA, 1947 ​(2008; Nouvelles Images S.A.; card). The delimiting punctuation is " :" (space-colon-space).] The controlled value of an attribute element can be displayed or otherwise output as a non-textual symbol. Examples Relation Example display of ISBDM metadata "Display the value "volume" of a has category of manifestation element as ." Relation Example display of ISBDM metadata "Display the value "microform" of a has media type element as ." The controlled values of a has category of manifestation element and element sub-types can be concatenated into a single compound value and displayed with or without a generic "category" label to simplify the display of a set of values. Examples Relation Example display of ISBDM metadata ""volume; unmediated; still image; text"" [Full example: Asterix and the gowden heuk ​(2014; Itchy Coo; volume). The delimiting punctuation is "; " (semicolon-space).] Relation Example display of ISBDM metadata ""Type: audiocassette - spoken word"" [Full example: Harry Potter and the goblet of fire ​(2000; Listening Library; audiocassette). The delimiting punctuation is " - " (space-hyphen-space). The value of has media type is omitted for clarity. "Type" is used as a generic display label.] The controlled values of a has creator agent of manifestation, has place of creation of manifestation, and has date of creation of manifestation elements and element sub-types can be concatenated into a single compound value and displayed with or without a generic "publication" label to simplify the display of a set of values. Examples Relation Example display of ISBDM metadata ""London (England) : Methuen Children’s Books, 1986"" [Full example: House at Pooh Corner ​(1986; Methuen Children’s Books; volume). The order of elements and delimiting punctuation conform to ISBD Area 4.] Relation Example display of ISBDM metadata ""Published: Cham (Switzerland); Springer (Cham, Switzerland); 2022-"" [Full example: Springer handbooks of political science and international relations ​(2022-; Springer; volume). The order of elements conforms to ISBD Area 4. The delimiting punctuation is "; " (semicolon-space). "Published" is used as a generic display label.]

This is a suggested order of presentation of element values for a "standard record" display: Representation of the manifestation. Transcribed values with relevant notes: has manifestation statement elements and element sub-types has note on manifestation statement elements and element sub-types Appellations of the manifestation. Controlled values and relevant notes: has nomen associated with manifestation elements and element sub-types has note on nomen associated with manifestation element Creation of the manifestation. Controlled values: has creator agent of manifestation elements and element sub-types has place of creation of manifestation elements and element sub-types has date of creation of manifestation elements and element sub-types Attributes of the manifestation. Controlled values with relevant notes: has category of manifestation element and element sub-types has note on category of manifestation element has physical characteristic element and element sub-types has note on physical characteristic element has use rights element and element sub-types Relationships with other manifestations. Controlled values with relevant notes: has manifestation associated with manifestation element and element sub-types has note on manifestation associated with manifestation element Relationships with other resource entities. Controlled values with relevant notes: has expression associated with manifestation element and element sub-types has note on expression associated with manifestation element has work associated with manifestation element and element sub-types has note on work associated with manifestation element has item associated with manifestation element and element sub-types has note on item associated with manifestation element Relationships with other agents. Controlled values with relevant notes: has distributor agent element and element sub-types has collective agent associated with manifestation element has person associated with manifestation element has agent associated with manifestation element has note on agent associated with manifestation element Relationships with other places and time-spans. Controlled values with relevant notes: has place associated with manifestation element and element sub-types has note on place associated with manifestation element has time-span associated with manifestation element and element sub-types has note on time-span associated with manifestation element This is a suggested order of specific elements within the suggested order of presentation. In general, elements are ordered from fine to broad granularity within a hierarchy. 1. Representation of the manifestation​ has manifestation statement of title and responsibility has note on manifestation statement of title and responsibility has manifestation statement of edition has note on manifestation statement of edition has manifestation statement of issue or iteration has note on manifestation statement of issue or iteration has manifestation statement of publication, production, manufacture, or distribution has note on manifestation statement of publication, production, manufacture, or distribution has manifestation statement of identifier and terms of availability has note on manifestation statement of identifier and terms of availability has manifestation statement of category has note on manifestation statement of category has manifestation statement of extent has note on manifestation statement of extent has manifestation statement has note on manifestation statement 2. Appellations of the manifestation​ has title proper has variant title of manifestation has title of manifestation has authorized access point of manifestation has variant access point of manifestation has access point of manifestation has catalogue number has publisher number has chronological designation has numeric designation has fingerprint has plate number has uniform resource locator has identifier of manifestation has nomen associated with manifestation has note on nomen associated with manifestation 3. Creation of the manifestation​ has publisher collective agent has publisher person has publisher agent has producer collective agent has producer person has producer agent has manufacturer collective agent has manufacturer person has manufacturer agent has creator collective agent of manifestation has creator person of manifestation has creator agent of manifestation has place of publication has place of production has place of manufacture has place of creation of manifestation has date of publication has date of production has date of manufacture has date of copyright of manifestation has date of creation of manifestation 4. Attributes of the manifestation​ has category of carrier has media type has category of embodied content has category of manifestation has note on category of manifestation has unitary structure has binding has encoding format has equalization has frame alignment has layout of embodied content has manufacturing process has applied material has base material has material has noise reduction has playing speed has recording method has regional encoding has track configuration has physical characteristic has note on physical characteristic has intended audience of manifestation has terms of availability has use rights has extent of manifestation has bibliographic format has dimensions has number of recording tracks has extent of unit has extent of unitary structure has designation of number of sound channels has number of sound channels has image resolution has playing time has reduction ratio has extent of embodied content has extent of aggregated content has note on manifestation 5. Relationships with other manifestations​ has sub-unit has super-unit has alternate manifestation has manifestation reproduced by manifestation has manifestation that reproduces manifestation has manifestation associated with manifestation has note on manifestation associated with manifestation 6. Relationships with other resource entities​ has expression embodied in manifestation has expression associated with manifestation has note on expression associated with manifestation has work embodied in manifestation has work associated with manifestation has note on work associated with manifestation has item that exemplifies manifestation has item reproduced by manifestation has item associated with manifestation has note on item associated with manifestation 7. Relationships with agents​ has distributor collective agent has distributor person has distributor agent has collective agent associated with manifestation has person associated with manifestation has agent associated with manifestation has note on agent associated with manifestation 8. Relationships with other places and time-spans​ has place of distribution has place associated with manifestation has note on place associated with manifestation has date of distribution has time-span associated with manifestation has note on time-span associated with manifestation

This is a suggested string encoding scheme for a value of a has extent of manifestation element. The string encoding scheme combines values of the element sub-types in the following order: has extent of unitary structure has extent of unit has extent of aggregated content has extent of embodied content The ISBDM string template is: {has extent of unitary structure} + "(" + {has extent of unit} + "; " + {has extent of aggregated content} + " in " + {has extent of embodied content} + ")" The boilerplate string " in " is a short form of " embodied in ". Examples Relation Example has extent of manifestation "3 volumes (124 leaves; 150 photographs in 200 pages)" has extent of manifestation "3 volumes (150 photographs in 200 pages)" has extent of manifestation "3 volumes (200 pages)" For a manifestation that has no sub-units, use the string that is the number "1" followed by a value for the has category of carrier element as a substitute for a value of has extent of unitary structure. Examples Relation Example has extent of manifestation "1 list (70 x 50 cm; 1 plakat na 70 x 50 cm)" Full example: Zadar does Banksy ​(2023; Narodni muzej Zadar; list) For a manifestation that is a super-unit, a string encoding scheme may combine values of element sub-types for sub-units of the manifestation. Examples Relation Example has extent of manifestation "1 volume (122 pages) + 1 audio disc (15 performed songs in 49 min 14 sec)" Full example: Mojo 357 ​(2023; H Bauer Publishing Ltd.; volume + audio disc) For a manifestation that embodies only one expression, use the string that is the number "1" followed by a value for the has category of embodied content element or a controlled term for a finer level of granularity of the category as a substitute for a value of has extent of aggregated content. Examples Relation Example has extent of manifestation "3 volumes (1 text in 363 pages)" Full example: Emma ​(1815; John Murray; volume). The manifestation is a single novel that is embodied in three volumes Relation Example has extent of manifestation "1 hartë" Full example: Corso delli fiumi Drino, e Boiana nella Dalmatia ​(2011; Biblioteka Kombëtare e Shqipërisë; burim online)

This is a suggested string encoding scheme for a value of a has title of manifestation element that is a compound title. For a manifestation that has a super-unit, the string encoding scheme combines values of strings that are taken from statements of title and responsibility that appear in the manifestation, in the following order: The component strings are separate by a colon and space ": ". The ISBDM string template is: [common title] + ": " + [unit designation} + ": " + [unit title] Examples Relation Example has title proper "Homazh për De Radën: DVD 1" Full example: Homazh për De Radën: DVD 1 ​(2004; Università della Calabria; videodisk). The value uses a common title and a unit designation; there is no unit title Relation Example has variant title of manifestation "New scientist. The collection: Vol three / issue three: The quantum world" Full example: Quantum world ​(2016; Reed Business Information Ltd; volume). The value uses a common title, a unit designation, and a unit title For a manifestation that is an aggregate, the string encoding scheme combines values of strings that are titles of distinct expressions or works that are taken from statements of title and responsibility that appear in the manifestation, in the order of appearance. The component strings are separate by a space, plus sign, and space " + ". The ISBDM string template is: [first title of expression] + " +: " + [second title of expression} + " + " + [third title of expression] … Examples Relation Example has title proper "Voyage extraordinaire au coeur de l'atome Voyage extraordinaire aux limites de l'univers" | | has title proper | "Voyage extraordinaire aux limites de l'univers + Voyage extraordinaire au coeur de l'atome" | Full example: Voyage extraordinaire au coeur de l'atome + Voyage extraordinaire aux limites de l'univers ​(1996; Editions Casterman; volume). The values use the distinct titles of expressions that are embodied in the manifestation in a tête-bêche layout.

This is a set of suggested string encoding schemes for authorized access points for the manifestation and related entities that are applied to the Examples in ISBD for Manifestation. The sources of component strings, their order, added punctuation, and added boilerplate strings are given in an ISBDM string template. The source of a component string that is an ISBDM element is given as an element name in curly brackets "". For example, "{has title proper}". The source of a component string that is not an ISBDM element is given in square brackets "[]". For example, "[supplied title]" An action that is applied to a component string is named and followed by the component string enclosed in round brackets "()". For example, "normalised({has title proper})" A choice of sources of a component string is indicated by a vertical bar "|" and given in order of availability. For example, "{has title proper}|[supplied title]". Added punctuation and boilerplate strings are given in quotation marks "". For example, "; ". The concatenation of component strings is indicated by a sign of addition "+". For example, "{has category of carrier} + ")"". A value of an element sub-type may be used as the source of a component string. A value of a component string should be normalised to ensure consistent collocation and display. Normalisation of a name or title value removes a leading definite or indefinite article. The suggested string encoding schemes for entities are: Agent SES Collective Agent SES Expression SES Item SES Manifestation SES Person SES Place SES Time-span SES Work SES The suggested string encoding schemes for elements are: Chronological designation SES Compound title SES Extent of manifestation SES Numeric designation SES

This is a suggested string encoding scheme for a value of a has chronological designation element. For a manifestation that embodies the expression of a diachronic work, a value for the first chronological designation in the sequence is followed by a hyphen "-" to indicate an open sequence. The ISBDM string template is: first in sequence({has chronological designation}) + "-" Examples Relation Example has chronological designation "2009-" Full example: Journal für Facility Management ​(2009-; Technische Universität Wien‏; online resource) For a manifestation that embodies the expression of a diachronic work, and if there is a change in the sequence of chronological designations of issues or iterations, values for the first and last chronological designations in the old sequence are separated by a hyphen "-" to indicate sequence range, followed by a value for new open sequence. Sequences are separated with semi-colons "; ". The ISBDM string template is: first in old sequence({has chronological designation}) + "-" + last in old sequence({has chronological designation}) + "; " + first in new sequence({has chronological designation}) + "-" For a manifestation that embodies the expression of a diachronic work that is known or assumed to have terminated, values for the first and last chronological designations in the sequence are separated by a hyphen "-" to indicate sequence range. The ISBDM string template is: first in sequence({has chronological designation}) + "-" + last in sequence({has chronological designation})

This is a suggested string encoding scheme for a value of a has numeric designation element. For a manifestation that embodies the expression of a diachronic work, a value for the first numeric designation in the sequence is followed by a hyphen "-" to indicate an open sequence. The ISBDM string template is: first in sequence({has numeric designation}) + "-" Examples Relation Example has numeric designation "Heft 1-" Full example: Journal für Facility Management ​(2009-; Technische Universität Wien‏; online resource) Relation Example has numeric designation "Lecture #1-" Full example: Synthesis lectures on data, semantics, and knowledge ​(2021-; Morgan & Claypool Publishers; volume) For a manifestation that embodies the expression of a diachronic work, and if there is a change in the sequence of numeric designations of issues or iterations, values for the first and last numeric designations in the old sequence are separated by a hyphen "-" to indicate sequence range, followed by a value for new open sequence. Sequences are separated with semi-colons "; ". The ISBDM string template is: first in old sequence({has numeric designation}) + "-" + last in old sequence({has numeric designation}) + "; " + first in new sequence({has numeric designation}) + "-" For a manifestation that embodies the expression of a diachronic work that is known or assumed to have terminated, values for the first and last numeric designations in the sequence are separated by a hyphen "-" to indicate sequence range. The ISBDM string template is: first in sequence({has numeric designation}) + "-" + last in sequence({has numeric designation})

This is a suggested string encoding scheme for an authorized access point of an agent who is related to the manifestation. The encoding scheme is applicable to the value of a has agent associated with manifestation element or element sub-type. For an agent who is a collective agent, apply the Collective Agent SES. For an agent who is a person, apply the Person SES. For any agent, add a qualifier that indicates that the agent is a collective agent or a person.

This is a suggested string encoding scheme for an authorized access point of a collective agent who is related to the manifestation. The encoding scheme is applicable to the value of a has collective agent associated with manifestation element or element sub-type. The base access point of a collective agent is a name of the collective agent that is the most common in external sources of information. The base access point may be followed by a set of qualifiers enclosed in brackets "(…)" and separated by semicolons "; ". The ISBDM string template is: [name of the collective agent] + " (" + [qualifier] + "; " + [qualifier] + ")" Add qualifiers to disambiguate the base access point. Added qualifiers are conditional on specific characteristics of the collective agent. They support a secondary collocation and sort order of authorized access points. Use the following strings as qualifiers of a base access point: A controlled term for a category of the collective agent A field of activity of the collective agent A period of activity of the collective agent, including the date of a conference, meeting, or voyage A place of activity of the collective agent, including the location of a conference, meeting, or voyage. A number or other sequence designator of a conference, meeting, or voyage Examples Relation Example has publisher collective agent "Thames & Hudson" Full example: Charles Rennie Mackintosh ​(2002; Thames & Hudson; volume; perfect binding). The base access point is not qualified Relation Example has publisher collective agent "Springer (Firm)" Full example: Synthesis lectures on data, semantics, and knowledge ​(2021-; Morgan & Claypool Publishers; volume). The base access point is qualified by a category of collective agent

This is a suggested string encoding scheme for an authorized access point of an expression that is related to the manifestation. The encoding scheme is applicable to the value of a has expression associated with manifestation element or element sub-type. The base access point of an expression is an authorized access point of the work that is realised by the expression. The base access point is followed by at least one qualifier that is added to the qualifiers of the authorized access point of the work, if any, and separated by a semicolon "; ". The ISBDM string template is: [authorized access point of the work] + insert before ")"("; " + [a category of content of the expression]) The qualifier supports a local secondary collocation and sort order of authorized access points of expressions in a browse index for expressions. Examples Relation Example has expression embodied in manifestation "Bonnard, Pierre, 1867-1947. Café (still image)" Full example: Coffee ​(2003; Tate; card) Relation Example has expression embodied in manifestation "Blythe, Ronald, 1922-2023. Introduction (Emma; text; English)" Full example: Emma ​(1971; Penguin Books; volume). The authorized access point of the work is qualified by the preferred title of an augmented work before it is further qualified as an authorized access point of the expression. Add qualifiers to the sequence to disambiguate the basic qualified access point. Added qualifiers are conditional on specific characteristics of the expression that are recorded as attribute elements. They support a tertiary collocation and sort order of authorized access points. Examples Relation Example has expression embodied in manifestation "The Beatles. Eleanor Rigby (performed music; 2022 stereo mix)" has expression embodied in manifestation "The Beatles. Eleanor Rigby (performed music; take 2)" Full example: Revolver ​(2022; Apple Corps Limited; audio disc; 2 CD edition). The base access point is an authorized access point of work that is qualified with a category of content and then qualified for disambiguation by a version. Qualify a value of a category of content of the expression that is "spoken word", "tactile text", or "text" with a value of a language of the expression. Examples Relation Example has expression embodied in manifestation "McCall Smith, Alexander, 1948-. Emma (text; English)" Full example: Emma ​(2014 ; Borough Press; volume; case binding) Relation Example has expression embodied in manifestation "Dib, Mohammed, 1920-2003. Incendie (texte; français)" Full example: Incendie ​(1954; Éditions du Seuil; volume; livre broché) Relation Example has expression embodied in manifestation "Rowling, J.K., 1965-. Harry Potter and the goblet of fire (spoken word; English)" Full example: Harry Potter and the goblet of fire ​(2000; Listening Library; audiocassette) Relation Example has expression embodied in manifestation "Jacques Meuris, 1923-1993. René Magritte (text; text; English)" Full example: René Magritte ​(2007; Taschen; volume). The base access point is an authorized access point of work that is qualified by a value of a category of content of a representative expression. The base qualified access point is qualified for disambiguation and then qualified by a category of content of the expression. Add a qualifier to the sequence to disambiguate the access point that is the authorized access point of an agent who is a creator of the expression but who is not a creator of the work that is realized by the expression. Examples Relation Example has expression embodied in manifestation "Milne, Alan Alexander, 1882-1956, Winnie-the-Pooh (tekst; hrvatski; Pervan, Mia)" Full example: Medo Winnie zvani Pooh ​(1986; Mladost; svezak). The base access point is an authorized access point of work that is qualified with a category of content and a language and then qualified for disambiguation by an authorized access point of a translator.

This is a suggested string encoding scheme for an authorized access point of an item that is related to the manifestation. The encoding scheme is applicable to the value of a has item associated with manifestation element or element sub-type. The base access point of an item is a value of has authorized access point of manifestation. The base access point is followed by a qualifier that is added to the qualifiers of the access point and separated by a semicolon "; ". The ISBDM string template is: {has authorized access point of manifestation} + insert before ")"("; " + [an identifier or shelfmark of the item]) The qualifier supports a local secondary collocation and sort order of authorized access points of manifestations in a browse index for items. Examples Relation Example has item reproduced by manifestation "Evangelistarium Marci Maruli Spalatensis (1519; Officina Adamae Petri; svezak; tvrdi uvez; HR-ZaNSK, RIIF-8o-416)" Full example: Evangelistarium Marci Maruli Spalatensis ​(201-; Nacionalna i sveučilišna knjižnica u Zagrebu; online jedinica građe) Relation Example has item reproduced by manifestation "Libar Marca Marula Splichianina Uchomse vsdarsi Istoria Sfete vdouice Judit u versih haruacchi slosena (1522; Mirković, Jerolim; svezak; HR-ZaNSK, RIIC-8o-100 primj. a)" Full example: Libar Marca Marula Splichianina Uchomse vsdarsi Istoria Sfete vdouice Judit u versih haruacchi slosena ​(1522; Mirković, Jerolim ; svezak) Relation Example has item that exemplifies manifestation "Burleska pro klarinet a klavír (1945-03-26; Vostřák, Zbyněk; sheet; Library of Congress Music Division, ML96 .V67 no. 1 case)" Full example: Burleska pro klarinet a klavír ​(1945-03-26; Vostřák, Zbyněk; sheet)

This is a suggested string encoding scheme for an authorized access point of the manifestation and of a manifestation that is related to the manifestation. The encoding scheme is applicable to the value of a has access point of manifestation element or element sub-type or a has manifestation associated with manifestation element or element sub-type. The encoding scheme uses values that are based on the elements that indicate that a manifestation is distinct. See also: Manifestation boundaries. The base access point of a manifestation is a normalized value of has title proper. If there is no such value, a title supplied by the cataloguing agency may be used. The base access point is followed by a set of qualifiers enclosed in brackets "(...)" and separated by semicolons "; ". The ISBDM string template is: normalised({has title proper})|[supplied title] + " (" + {has date of creation of manifestation}|{has date of copyright of manifestation} + "; " + {has creator agent of manifestation} + "; " + {has category of carrier} + ")" If a value of a qualifier is not known, omit the qualifier from the access point. If a qualifier has more than one value, use a concatenation of the values separated by " + " (space-plus-space). Order the values by prominence and quantity. The sequence of qualifiers supports a standard secondary collocation and sort order of authorized access points in a browse index for manifestations. Examples Relation Example has authorized access point of manifestation "Desserte rouge 1908 (1993; Editions du Centre Pompidou; sheet)" Full example: Desserte rouge 1908 ​(1993; Editions du Centre Pompidou; sheet) Relation Example has authorized access point of manifestation "Corso delli fiumi Drino, e Boiana nella Dalmatia (1688; fletë)" Full example: Corso delli fiumi Drino, e Boiana nella Dalmatia ​(1688; fletë). The publisher is not known Relation Example has authorized access point of manifestation "Съкровищница (2018; Народна библиотека "Св. св. Кирил и Методий"; том + компютърен диск)" Full example: Съкровищница ​(2018; Народна библиотека "Св. св. Кирил и Методий"; том + компютърен диск). The manifestation has sub-units that have different categories of carrier Add qualifiers to the sequence to disambiguate the basic qualified access point. Added qualifiers are conditional on specific characteristics of the manifestation that are recorded as attribute elements. They support a tertiary collocation and sort order of authorized access points. Qualify a value of has category of carrier that is "volume" with a value of has binding. Examples Relation Example has authorized access point of manifestation "Paris apartment (2022; HarperCollinsPublishers; volume; case binding)" Full example: Paris apartment ​(2022; HarperCollinsPublishers; volume; case binding) Relation Example has authorized access point of manifestation "Biographical dictionary of Scottish women (2007; Edinburgh University Press; volume; perfect binding)" Full example: Biographical dictionary of Scottish women ​(2007; Edinburgh University Press; volume; perfect binding) Qualify a value of has category of carrier that is "online resource" with a value of has encoding format. Examples Relation Example has authorized access point of manifestation "Emma (1994; Project Gutenberg; online resource; plain text format)" has alternate manifestation "Emma (1994; Project Gutenberg; online resource; HTML format)" has alternate manifestation "Emma (1994; Project Gutenberg; online resource; EPUB3 format)" has alternate manifestation "Emma (1994; Project Gutenberg; online resource; EPUB format)" has alternate manifestation "Emma (1994; Project Gutenberg; online resource; Kindle format)" Full example: Emma ​(1994; Project Gutenberg; online resource; plain text format) Qualify a value of has category of carrier that is "videodisc" with a controlled term for a finer level of granularity of the category of carrier. Examples Relation Example has authorized access point of manifestation "Einstein on the beach (2016; Opus Arte; videodisc; DVD)" has alternate manifestation "Einstein on the beach (2016; Opus Arte; videodisc; BD)" Full example: Einstein on the beach ​(2016; Opus Arte; videodisc; DVD) Qualify a value of has title proper that is a generic title with an authorized access point of an agent who is responsible for the creation of works and expressions that are embodied in the manifestation. Examples Relation Example has authorized access point of manifestation "Summary records (Unesco. Executive Board. 215th session; 2022; Paris) (2023; Unesco Executive Board; svezak)" Apply the same string encoding scheme to an authorized access point of a related manifestation.

This is a suggested string encoding scheme for an authorized access point of a person who is related to the manifestation. The encoding scheme is applicable to the value of a has person associated with manifestation element or element sub-type. The base access point of a person is a name of the person that is the most common in external sources of information. Apply the guidance for the language or country of origin of the name that is available in Names of persons, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. For a name of a person that includes a family name, transpose the family part of the name to the beginning so that the base appears in a browse index in order of the family name. The base access point may be followed by a set of qualifiers enclosed in brackets "(…)" and separated by semicolons "; ". The ISBDM string template is: transposed([name of the person]) + " (" + [qualifier] + "; " + [qualifier] + ")" Add qualifiers to disambiguate the base access point. Added qualifiers are conditional on specific characteristics of the person. They support a secondary collocation and sort order of authorized access points. Use the following strings as qualifiers of a base access point: The date of birth of the person in a standard format The date of death of the person in a standard format A profession, occupation, or field of activity of the person A period of activity that is associated with the profession, occupation, or field of activity of the person Examples Relation Example has person associated with manifestation "Magritte, René, 1898-1967" Full example: Treachery of images ​(ceci n'est pas une pipe) ​(1929; Magritte, René, 1898-1967; sheet). The base access point is transposed and is qualified by the dates of birth and death

This is a suggested string encoding scheme for an authorized access point of a place that is related to the manifestation. The encoding scheme is applicable to the value of a has place associated with manifestation element or element sub-type. The base access point of a place is a name of the place that is the most common in external sources of information. The base access point may be followed by a set of qualifiers enclosed in brackets "(...)" and separated by semicolons "; ". The ISBDM string template is: [name of the place] + " (" + [qualifier] + "; " + [qualifier] + ")" Add qualifiers to disambiguate the base access point. Added qualifiers are conditional on specific characteristics of the place. They support a secondary collocation and sort order of authorized access points. Use the following strings as qualifiers of a base access point: A name of a larger place that includes the place A category of place Examples Relation Example has place of publication "Edinburgh (Scotland)" Full example: Asterix and the gowden heuk ​(2014; Itchy Coo; volume). The base access point is qualified by the name of a larger place. Relation Example has place of publication "Alger (Algerie)" Full example: Algerie a travers les ages ​(2000; Cerist; disque informatique; version française). The base access point is qualified by the name of a larger place.

This is a suggested string encoding scheme for an authorized access point of a time-span that is related to the manifestation. The encoding scheme is applicable to the value of a has time-span associated with manifestation element or element sub-type. The base access point of a time-span is a name of the time-span that is the most common in external sources of information. {name of the time-span} The base access point may be followed by a set of qualifiers enclosed in brackets "(…)" and separated by semicolons "; ". The ISBDM string template is: [name of the time-span] + " (" + [qualifier] + "; " + [qualifier] + ")" Add qualifiers to disambiguate the base access point. Added qualifiers are conditional on specific characteristics of the time-span. They support a secondary collocation and sort order of authorized access points. Use the following strings as qualifiers of a base access point: A category of time-span

This is a suggested string encoding scheme for an authorized access point of a work that is related to the manifestation. The encoding scheme is applicable to the value of a has work associated with manifestation element or element sub-type. The base access point of a work is a combination of a value of an authorized access point of a creator agent of the work and a value of a preferred title of the work. The ISBDM string template is: [authorized access point of a creator agent of the work] + ". " + [preferred title of the work] For a work that is anonymous, apply the guidance for the language or country of origin of the name that is available in Anonymous classics, if it is considered to be useful for users of the metadata. The base access point may be followed by a set of qualifiers enclosed in brackets "(...)" and separated by semicolons "; ". Add qualifiers to the sequence to disambiguate the basic qualified access point. Added qualifiers are conditional on specific characteristics of the work that are recorded as attribute elements, including representative expression attributes. They support a tertiary collocation and sort order of authorized access points. Examples Relation Example has work embodied in manifestation "Bonnard, Pierre, 1867-1947. Café" Full example: Coffee ​(2003; Tate; card). The base access point is not qualified. Relation Example has work embodied in manifestation "Gayford, Martin, 1952-. Spring cannot be cancelled (text)" Full example: Spring cannot be cancelled ​(2022; Thames & Hudson; volume). The base access point is qualified by a value of a category of content of a representative expression. For a work that is an augmenting work that is embodied in an aggregate manifestation, and if the preferred title of the work is a generic title, qualify the base access point with a preferred title of the augmented work. Examples Relation Example has work associated with manifestation "Blythe, Ronald, 1922-2023. Introduction (Emma)" The work augments another work that is embodied in the same manifestation.
